feature-36d716a4.note: At the parent the new tests/unit_tests/test_structured_recipe_times_migration.py fails at collection (its module-level glob finds no migration), and the selector runs all seven files in one pytest session, which then aborts. That is why every test in those files is a target, including many the commit did not touch (other cleaner helpers, SPA serving, the rest of the AI import, the other migrators, schema coercion); the request states those as behaviours to keep instead of restating each unrelated case. The migration test imports five helpers straight from the migration module, so their names, argument order and exact parsing rules are given, with the revision id, down revision, message and create date; the file name is left to alembic.ini's file_template rather than spelled as a changed path. The parsing rules differ on purpose between the migration (whole seconds only, no rounding, unit words from every locale) and clean_duration (rounds to the nearest second, ISO or bare minutes only), and clean_time must treat 'PT' as a zero duration (None) yet keep 'P1M', '-PT1H' and 'PT-3H' as text, so exact values are listed. test_clean_scraper_structures_times runs cleaner.clean after clean_scraper, so the request states the end result of scraping, not which function produces the seconds. The migrator expectations depend on the test archives, so each recipe is named with its source values. The frontend spec checks German by regex and the en-US short names 'hr'/'min', which in practice needs the platform's Intl unit formatting; the request says unit names come from Intl, which is close to a hint, but nothing else passes it. The cleaner and SPA modules are described by the functions they hold, not by their dotted names; RecipeModel, RecipeSummary, OpenAIRecipe and RecipeScraperPackage.clean_scraper are named as symbols.

feature-4a280cbd.note: The integration tests import the auth routes module and patch its module-level `settings` object (REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_HEADER, REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SECRET, REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED) and replace REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_READY on that object's class with a property. Meanwhile the provider unit tests drive settings through environment variables plus get_app_settings.cache_clear(). The request therefore states four things: the endpoint reads from that module-level object; READY is a property on the settings class, not a field (monkeypatch would fail on a pydantic field); the provider reads get_app_settings() at call time; and the provider must not re-check REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_ENABLED, which is unset in the integration tests. The unit test imports ReverseProxyProvider from a new module (mealie.core.security.providers.reverse_proxy_provider). Since that is a changed file, the request places it by its package and by its siblings' naming convention instead of spelling out the module name. The Alembic migration matters only on Postgres, and no test depends on its revision id (upstream used f3a8b6c1d2e4 revising 3697d65c5f92). The status-reporting fields in point 5 are part of the upstream change but are not asserted; they are described briefly.

They come from the progress keys declared on DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_STEPS/DEFAULT_SOURCE_COMPILERS, and from quoted 'recipe.create-progress.*'/'recipe.import-errors.*' literals scanned across mealie/**/*.py. The en-US texts of the new keys are not asserted (the tests compare against translator.t), so they are paraphrased. The merge format (labels, preamble) is not tested, so only its behaviour is described. Many tests in the target files are unchanged; they are listed under 'must keep working' because the refactor could plausibly break them.

An empty Location is now followed up to the cap (4 requests) instead of stopping at once. That is counterintuitive but asserted, so the request states it. Every test in the hidden files is a target, including the unchanged OIDC claim tests, recipe-action and webhook CRUD, and the fetch-loop tests. All recipe-action tests fail at the parent only because their autouse fixture patches safehttp.post, which did not exist. The existing fetch tests replace get_app_settings with a namespace that lacks the new lists while also replacing _build_transport, hence the sentence that only _build_transport reads the lists.
